clause_text: Under Section 2(7), a 'Consumer' is any person who buys goods or hires services for consideration, but excludes anyone who obtains goods for resale or commercial purposes.
Under Section 2(10), a 'Defect' means any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in quality, quantity, potency, purity, or standard required by law or contract.
Under Section 2(11), a 'Deficiency' means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming, or inadequacy in the quality, nature, and manner of performance of a service.
Under Section 2(47), an 'Unfair Trade Practice' includes false representation of goods, misleading warranty claims, failure to issue bill/cash memo, and refusing to take back defective goods.
Under Section 2(28), misleading advertisements falsely describe products, give false guarantees, or deliberately conceal important information from consumers.
Consumers have the right to be protected against marketing of goods, products, and services that are hazardous to life and property.
Consumers have the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard, and price of goods or services to prevent unfair practices.
Consumers have the right to be assured access to a variety of goods and services at competitive prices wherever possible.
Consumers have the right to be heard and assured that their interests will receive due consideration in appropriate consumer forums.
Consumers have the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices or exploitation, and the right to consumer awareness and education.
Under Section 10, the Central Government establishes the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to protect, promote, and enforce consumer rights as a class.
Under Section 20, the CCPA has the statutory power to order recall of dangerous goods, refund of prices paid, and discontinuation of unfair trade practices.
Under Section 21, the CCPA can impose penalties up to ₹10 Lakhs on manufacturers and endorsers for misleading ads, rising up to ₹50 Lakhs for subsequent violations.
The CCPA can prohibit a celebrity endorser of a misleading advertisement from making any endorsement for up to 1 year, and up to 3 years for subsequent violations.
Under Section 34, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission entertains complaints where the value of goods or services paid does not exceed ₹50 Lakhs.
Under Section 47, the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission entertains complaints where value exceeds ₹50 Lakhs but does not exceed ₹2 Crores.
Under Section 58, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) entertains complaints where the value exceeds ₹2 Crores.
Under Section 69, a consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date on which the cause of action arose.
Under Section 41, any person aggrieved by an order of the District Commission may prefer an appeal to the State Commission within 45 days from the date of the order.
Complaints filed in the District Commission with claims up to ₹5 Lakhs are completely exempt from paying any court or application fee.
Every e-commerce entity must appoint a nodal grievance officer and acknowledge consumer complaints within 48 hours.
E-commerce entities must resolve consumer grievances within 1 month (30 days) from the date of receipt of the complaint.
E-commerce platforms must clearly display the country of origin, expiry date, manufacturer details, and total price with breakup for all listed goods.
E-commerce sellers cannot impose cancellation charges on consumers unless similar charges are borne by the seller for unilateral cancellations.
E-commerce entities are prohibited from organizing fraudulent flash sales or back-to-back sales that limit consumer choice or artificially inflate prices.
Under Section 84, a product manufacturer is liable in a product liability action if the product has a manufacturing defect, defective design, or lacks adequate warning instructions.
Under Section 85, a product service provider is liable for harm caused if the service provided was deficient, negligent, or violated safety standards.
Under Section 74, the State Government establishes Consumer Mediation Cells attached to District and State Commissions to resolve disputes through voluntary mediation.
Under Section 72, failure to comply with an order of the District, State, or National Commission is punishable with imprisonment between 1 month to 3 years, or fine from ₹25,000 to ₹1 Lakh, or both.
Under Section 35, where the Commission finds a complaint to be frivolous or vexatious, it may dismiss the complaint and order the complainant to pay costs up to ₹50,000 to the opposite party.
